description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:636 — `let mut fn_ = proof.leaf_index;` — the name `fn_` is chosen because `fn` is a Rust keyword. The whole verify_inclusion_inner function uses `fn_` and `sn` (the RFC 9162 §2.1.3.2 notation: leaf_index becomes fn, tree_size-1 becomes sn). Mathematical notation matters in this algorithm — it makes the per-iteration invariants easy to check against the RFC.

But `fn_` is jarring. Suggested rename: `f` (for "fn" without the keyword collision) or `idx` (matches Rust idiom) or `node_idx`. The RFC notation is preserved in a comment block at the top of the function showing the variable mapping.

This is taste — the existing code is correct and the RFC-notation match is genuine. Marked opinion. Listing only because the convention currently puts an underscore-suffix on an internal variable that has no other namesake to disambiguate from. If anything is to change, simpler to drop to `f` than to keep `fn_`.
title: fn_ variable name in verify_inclusion_inner is awkward — fn is a keyword so the trailing underscore reads as a hack
